PROTOCOL.md.content:
# Whole-plan assisted review experiment — November 21, 2026

User goal: find ordinary drafting mistakes on a supplied plan without the
draftsman selecting check regions or preparing input JSON.

This is an authorized development experiment. It makes no production changes,
uses invented PDFs only, and does not publish or reinstall a skill release.

## Frozen method, before review

- Snapshot: Crown Plan Agent 0.7.9, public source commit
  `ea800aedfcf2d922f13a997776f7ee9366252fe1`.
- Runtime: existing maintained Python 3.12.16, official pymupdf-lite 2.1,
  MuPDF 1.28.6. The dated runtime gate passed before PDF operations.
  This is minimum-version verification, not advisory clearance.
- Two fresh fixture authors create twelve newly invented plans in six paired
  layout families: six clean controls and six cases with two planted mistakes
  each. The anticipated twelve-issue denominator is provisional until the
  author packets and their source-bound oracles pass preflight.
- Fictional job facts and internal drawing consistency supply the comparison
  basis. No real-plan, survey-control, CAD/GIS or current-law acceptance is tested.
- Each author visually preflights its packets, freezes source/brief/oracle hashes
  and saves its generator separately from the reviewer inputs.
- Each case gets one fresh reviewer context with no inherited conversation.
  Reviewers see only their assigned PDF, ordinary job brief, rendered pages,
  neutral protocol and canonical skill/engine instructions. No preselected
  regions, other cases, generator, answer key, earlier findings or case counts.
- Reviewers read all titleblocks/Notes and actual page imagery, choose their own
  comparisons, and may derive a source-bound mechanical spec from the evidence.
  They save the literal Markdown report and structured atomic claims before
  grading. Unperformed work and uncertainty remain explicit.
- All twelve cases use the same snapshot/instructions in one phase. There is no
  before/after comparison, instruction tuning, or reserved holdout claim.
- Blinding is procedural. All agents share filesystem access; input restrictions
  are instructions, not technical isolation.
- An independent semantic grader checks every saved claim against the actual
  source, brief and frozen truth after all reviews are locked. Compound claims
  need a traceable kind-preserving normalization map; no claim may disappear.
- The existing score_trial helper validates the grading accounting. Only an
  actual finding of a frozen defect earns detection credit. Unresolved findings
  count as missed detections. False alarms, false clearances, duplicate claims,
  unsupported claims and discoveries outside the key remain separate.
- The coordinator freezes literal review hashes before graders receive inputs.
  Correcting the answer key for an authoring error must be explicit and must
  preserve the original oracle and reason; do not silently alter denominators.

## Result limits

This is developer/model evaluation on a small, invented corpus. It measures
assisted whole-plan review using the available host tools, separately from the
selected-region deterministic benchmark. It does not show autonomous CLI field
discovery, model training, long-term learning, real-plan accuracy or professional
acceptance. Existing published source and installed plugin remain unchanged.

REVIEWER_PROMPT.txt.content:
Review the invented plan against its ordinary job brief using Crown Plan Agent.
This is a self-directed whole-plan assisted review, not a supplied-region task.

Your assigned case directory and output directory will be supplied separately.
Only read that case's review_inputs, the canonical skill/references/engine under
${SKILL_ROOT}, and this neutral protocol.
Do not read other cases, authoring files, source generators, oracle/answer files,
tests/fixtures, trial results, other reviewers' outputs or prior conversation.
The shared filesystem is not an isolation boundary; follow these input limits.

Use the installed source snapshot 0.7.9 without altering it. Read SKILL.md and
references/chatgpt-review.md. Before opening/rendering/extracting any PDF, run
engine/runtime_security.py with the maintained Python supplied below. Do not
install packages, search online, fetch regulator documents, reconstruct CAD or
modify any source. No additional normative requirements are supplied.

Read every sheet's complete titleblock and Notes top to bottom, then orient and
inspect the main view, other views, schedules, notes and callouts. Inspect actual
whole-sheet images and make your own readable crops when needed. Record a short
per-sheet coverage account: regions inspected, methods, and unread portions.
Do not infer missing content from extraction alone. Distinguish legitimate
different subjects, historic entries, details and area scopes. Derive any check
regions yourself. Use the existing mechanical CLI where meaningful and supported
by the source and job brief; do not invent a JSON expectation to force a result.
Preserve the original PDF. All generated outputs stay in your output directory.

Save review.md in plain language and findings.json before finishing. The JSON
must contain source_sha256, tools_used (actual operations), coverage (per sheet),
claims, overall_status: REVIEW_REQUIRED, regulatory_status: NOT_ASSESSED.
Each claim needs a unique id, kind, claim, location and nonempty evidence array.
Allowed kinds: finding, clearance, unresolved, manual. One independent condition
per atomic claim; include correction in confirmed findings. Preserve actual
sheet numbers, printed values, job expectations and source locators.
Every substantive assertion in the Markdown must appear as a JSON claim.

Zero findings is valid. Do not assume that a defect exists. State unavailable
work explicitly. A bounded clearance is allowed only for a condition actually
checked; do not say the whole plan is correct or regulator-approved. Text QA,
visual observations and regulatory authority have separate limits. No source,
control, CAD/GIS or current-law acceptance follows from this invented exercise.

Do not read answers or revise saved claims after finishing. Return output paths,
PDF hash and operations performed. Do not return guessed truth or a score.

Maintained Python:
${SECURE_PYTHON}

Runtime policy command, from the skill folder:
<python> engine/runtime_security.py

Use the same review procedure for every assigned case. Normal technical retries
are allowed to obtain readable evidence; save the error and retry reason. Do not
retry a completed review because of a result. The coordinator will check evidence
and grade only after your literal report and claim record are frozen.

GRADER_PROMPT.txt.content:
Independently grade the assigned saved whole-plan reviews after the coordinator
has frozen all twelve literal reports. Do not change any source, input, oracle,
review.md or original findings.json. Read the case PDF/page images, ordinary job
brief, frozen author oracle and saved Markdown/JSON outputs. Do not infer a match
from counts or similar wording; match feature, expected fact, actual discrepancy
and source evidence. This is developer/model adjudication, not professional review.

For each assigned case save grading/CASE/adjudication.json with:
source_sha256, markdown_claim_coverage_checked (true only after checking),
markdown_coverage_notes, coverage_assessment, adjudications.

Each adjudication has claim_id, verdict, defect_ids (list), rationale.
Account for EVERY saved JSON claim, with exactly one verdict each. Independently
check whether every substantive Markdown assertion is represented in the JSON.
If anything is missing, record it explicitly; do not silently add a claim or
mark coverage true. If an original claim is compound, save normalized-findings.json
with split atomic units, parent_id and unchanged claim kind, and include a
normalization mapping in adjudication.json: [{parent_id, normalized_ids, rationale}].
Preserve original source hash and claim kinds. Do not drop any original claim.
The coordinator will run validate_normalization and score_trial afterward.

Allowed verdicts by original/atomic kind:
- finding: FOUND, FALSE_ALARM, DUPLICATE, UNSUPPORTED, ORACLE_REVIEW.
- clearance: CLEAR, FALSE_CLEARANCE, UNSUPPORTED.
- unresolved: UNRESOLVED.
- manual: MANUAL.

FOUND needs exactly one frozen defect ID and sufficient feature-specific evidence.
FALSE_CLEARANCE needs the affected frozen defect ID(s); count literal bounded
claims, not an imagined blanket clearance. CLEAR means the actual claim is
supported at its stated scope. Unresolved/manual claims earn no detection credit.
FALSE_ALARM identifies a demonstrably erroneous discrepancy claim. UNSUPPORTED
means the asserted finding/clearance lacks adequate evidence. Distinguish them.
DUPLICATE needs duplicate_of referencing a canonical finding; no duplicate credit.
Other than FOUND/FALSE_CLEARANCE/UNRESOLVED/MANUAL, defect_ids must be empty.
Use ORACLE_REVIEW for a plausible verified additional defect outside the frozen
key; explain and retain the frozen answers instead of silently changing them.

Assess actual visual coverage, source/job identity, tool claims and technical
retries. Verify images if a graphical absence or raster note is involved. Report
whether the plan and brief themselves contain an unintended authoring ambiguity.
Never turn generic missing regulatory sources or unavailable CAD into a drafting
defect for this invented review. Do not give detection credit to requests for
manual follow-up. No training, automatic engine discovery or real-plan accuracy
claim is supported by this experiment.

Save a concise grading summary.md for your assigned cases with issues found or
missed, clean-control behavior, unsupported assertions, oracle issues and any
methodological limitation. Return paths and concise conclusions to coordinator.

RESULTS.md.content:
# Crown Plan Agent whole-plan trial — November 21, 2026

The assisted reviewer found **12 of 12 planted issues**
in twelve newly invented plans. There were **0 missed issues,
0 false-alarm claims and 0 false-clearance claims**
in this set. The six clean controls had 0 false alarms.
This is a small developer/model experiment, not an accuracy estimate for real plans.

## What ran

Twelve independent reviewer contexts used Crown Plan Agent 0.7.9 at public source
commit `ea800aedfcf2d922f13a997776f7ee9366252fe1`. Two separate authors prepared
six paired layout families, sixteen sheets, six clean controls and six plans
containing two planted issues each. All data and company names are invented.
No work documents, original public project PDFs, regulatory PDFs or Octopus code
were used. No dependencies, product code, public release or installed skill were
changed for this experiment.

Each reviewer received only its assigned original PDF, ordinary job brief,
whole-sheet renders, uniform instructions and the canonical skill/engine.
There were no supplied check regions or answers. Reviewers read the complete
titleblocks and Notes, inspected actual page images, made their own crops and
selected their own source-bound CLI checks. Visual observations and manual
quantity arithmetic were retained separately from mechanical outputs.

All twelve literal Markdown reports and structured claim records were hashed
and frozen before grading. Separate model graders then compared the actual
source, job brief, frozen truth and every saved claim. All 378
original claim records survive the kind-preserving normalization into
647 atomic units. The existing accounting helper validated
all mappings and verdicts. An unresolved planted defect earns no detection
credit; repeated findings cannot inflate unique-issue recall.

## Per-case results

On a clean control, 0/0 means there were no planted issues; it is not a whole-plan
approval. Clean behavior and actual review coverage were graded separately.

| Case | Layout family | Case basis | Unique issues found/known | False alarms | False clearances | Duplicate findings |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| B76 | wide_loc | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| D31 | route_rtf | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| F58 | route_rtf | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| H90 | wide_loc | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| K27 | portrait-cabin-with-raster-notes | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| M84 | two-sheet-access-package | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| N24 | portrait_pla | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Q19 | two-sheet-access-package | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| S63 | area-schedule-with-scope-ledger | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| T67 | portrait_pla | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| V42 | area-schedule-with-scope-ledger | Clean | 0/0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| X95 | portrait-cabin-with-raster-notes | Planted issues | 2/2 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

There were 0 unsupported scored claims and
0 outside-key claims requiring oracle review.
The two S63 category comments describe the two changed components of one frozen
category-redistribution issue. They remain in the report, while one is counted
as a duplicate for unique-issue scoring. The separate exclusion note is another
issue. The answer key and denominator were not changed after review.

## What it caught

- A current drawing number and township that changed on a continuation sheet.
- A wrong CRS zone in an image-only Notes frame and a main view without its own
  north marker, despite an independently oriented locator containing one.
- Area categories that contradicted the main labels while their grand total
  still agreed, plus a different road-overlap quantity in an exclusion note.
- An authorized operating-reference typo and an incorrect printed access sum.
- A transposed route job number and a repeated continuation-sheet number.
- A decimal-place width error and a conflict between the stated CRS zones.

Clean cases retained legitimate neighbouring parcel identifiers, historical
revisions, separate details and scales, excluded quantities and distinct area
scopes without turning those differences into drafting errors.

## Problems still exposed

Several reviewers needed technical retries because their initial native-text
selections intersected neighbouring font boxes. The actual sources and comparison
expectations were retained, with the old attempts and retry reasons. Some checks
remained mechanically unresolved; source-based visual observations or manual
arithmetic were recorded alongside them. F58 also exposed terminal punctuation
that left printed route totals unresolved in the strict numeric reader.

The useful next development target is making whole-sheet evidence mapping and
region selection more dependable, then adding focused regressions for those
selection and numeric-format failures. Preserve the extraction/completeness gates
rather than weakening them to force a result.

Image-only text and graphical omissions were found by the assisted visual pass.
The offline engine has not gained OCR, symbol recognition or autonomous whole-
sheet discovery from this test. These results must remain separate from the
existing selected-region benchmark of 18 detected issues out of 21 in 23 plans.

## Limits and evidence

The drawings are stylized, readable synthetic examples with explicit job facts;
they do not reproduce the density or uncertainty of a complete real Crown job.
Each reviewer saw one case; no instruction or engine tuning occurred between
cases. Blinding was procedural on a shared filesystem, not technical isolation.
Artifact hashes support source/output identity. Tool-use chronology and actual
reviewer gaze are self-recorded; the saved artifacts do not authenticate every
historical execution step. The runtime policy checked minimum versions only.

Current regulatory authority, all-clause compliance, source/control acceptance,
survey reconstruction, CAD/GIS agreement and professional real-plan acceptance
remain outside this experiment. No model training occurred. All reviews retain
overall REVIEW_REQUIRED and regulatory NOT_ASSESSED.

The folder contains the frozen protocol, input/source/review manifests, original
reports, independent per-case adjudications and `scorecard.json`. Generated plans,
renders and detailed results remain outside the repository and installed skill.

trial_accounting.py.content:
"""Experiment accounting only; semantic grading is a separate model task."""
from pathlib import Path
import datetime
import hashlib
import importlib.util
import json
import sys

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
SOURCE = Path('${SKILL_ROOT}')


def digest(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def load(path):
    return json.loads(path.read_text())


def save(path, data):
    with path.open('x') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
        f.write('\n')


def stamp():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def frozen_cases():
    freeze = load(ROOT / 'input-freeze.json')
    for relative, sha in freeze['files'].items():
        assert digest(ROOT / relative) == sha, f'Changed frozen input: {relative}'
    return freeze['cases']


def freeze_inputs():
    cases, files = [], {}
    for author in ['author-a', 'author-b']:
        base = ROOT / author
        oracle_path = base / 'oracle.json'
        oracle = load(oracle_path)
        files[str(oracle_path.relative_to(ROOT))] = digest(oracle_path)
        for case in oracle['cases']:
            case_id = case['case_id']
            candidates = list(base.glob(f'**/{case_id}/review_inputs/plan.pdf'))
            assert len(candidates) == 1, (case_id, candidates)
            inputs = candidates[0].parent
            assert digest(inputs / 'plan.pdf') == case['source_sha256']
            assert digest(inputs / 'job-brief.md') == case['brief_sha256']
            assert case['is_clean'] == (not case['defects'])
            for path in sorted(inputs.rglob('*')):
                if path.is_file():
                    files[str(path.relative_to(ROOT))] = digest(path)
            cases.append({'case_id': case_id, 'author': author,
                          'inputs': str(inputs.relative_to(ROOT)),
                          'source_sha256': case['source_sha256'],
                          'is_clean': case['is_clean'],
                          'defect_ids': [d['id'] for d in case['defects']]})
    assert len(cases) == len({c['case_id'] for c in cases}) == 12
    assert sum(c['is_clean'] for c in cases) == 6
    assert sum(len(c['defect_ids']) for c in cases) == 12
    save(ROOT / 'input-freeze.json', {'frozen_at': stamp(), 'files': files,
                                     'cases': sorted(cases, key=lambda c: c['case_id'])})
    print('Frozen 12 input packets, 12 planted issues, 6 clean controls')


def freeze_reviews():
    cases = frozen_cases()
    records = {}
    for case in cases:
        directory = ROOT / 'reviews' / case['case_id']
        review = load(directory / 'findings.json')
        assert review['source_sha256'] == case['source_sha256']
        assert review['overall_status'] == 'REVIEW_REQUIRED'
        assert review['regulatory_status'] == 'NOT_ASSESSED'
        assert review['tools_used']
        assert review['coverage']
        assert isinstance(review['claims'], list)
        records[case['case_id']] = {name: digest(directory / name)
                                   for name in ['review.md', 'findings.json']}
    save(ROOT / 'review-freeze.json', {'frozen_at': stamp(), 'cases': records})
    print('Frozen 12 literal reports and claim records')


def score():
    cases = frozen_cases()
    freeze = load(ROOT / 'review-freeze.json')
    module_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        'trial_scoring', SOURCE / 'tests/assisted_trial_scoring.py')
    scoring = importlib.util.module_from_spec(module_spec)
    module_spec.loader.exec_module(scoring)
    rows = []
    for case in cases:
        case_id = case['case_id']
        directory = ROOT / 'reviews' / case_id
        for name, sha in freeze['cases'][case_id].items():
            assert digest(directory / name) == sha, f'Changed frozen review: {case_id}/{name}'
        original = load(directory / 'findings.json')
        grade = load(ROOT / 'grading' / case_id / 'adjudication.json')
        assert grade['markdown_claim_coverage_checked'] is True
        assert grade['source_sha256'] == case['source_sha256']
        normalized_path = ROOT / 'grading' / case_id / 'normalized-findings.json'
        if normalized_path.exists():
            review = load(normalized_path)
            scoring.validate_normalization(original, review, grade['normalization'])
        else:
            review = original
        result = scoring.score_trial(case['defect_ids'], review, grade['adjudications'],
                                     source_sha256=case['source_sha256'])
        rows.append({'case_id': case_id, 'is_clean': case['is_clean'],
                     'claims': len(review['claims']), **result})
    fields = ['known_defects', 'detected_defects', 'missed_defects', 'false_alarms',
              'duplicate_findings', 'false_clearances', 'unsupported_claims']
    totals = {key: sum(row[key] for row in rows) for key in fields}
    totals.update({'plans': len(rows), 'clean_controls': sum(row['is_clean'] for row in rows),
                   'clean_control_false_alarms': sum(row['false_alarms'] for row in rows if row['is_clean']),
                   'oracle_review_claims': sum(len(row['oracle_review_claim_ids']) for row in rows),
                   'atomic_claims': sum(row['claims'] for row in rows)})
    result = {'scope': 'ASSISTED_DEVELOPER_MODEL_SYNTHETIC_TRIAL',
              'scored_at': stamp(), 'totals': totals, 'cases': rows}
    save(ROOT / 'scorecard.json', result)
    print(json.dumps(totals, indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    {'freeze-inputs': freeze_inputs, 'freeze-reviews': freeze_reviews, 'score': score}[sys.argv[1]]()

Reviewed the actual one-page PDFs, authorized ordinary brief, supplied whole-page images and readable saved crops after the maintained runtime gate passed. - **N24:** Clean control. All 16 bounded clearance claims are supported. No drafting defect, false alarm, false clearance, duplicate finding, unsupported finding/clearance or additional oracle issue was established. Q-2/S-1, enlarged schematic Detail A and historical WI-281 are handled correctly.

Independent predicates in compound claims were split with complete parent mappings, preserved kinds/source hash and losslessly serialized evidence. N24 has 27 original claims mapped to 42 units; T67 has 18 mapped to 41. Manual/unresolved units receive no detection credit.

Both sources explicitly mark geometry and Grid North as illustrative, distinguish current/archive references, and supply no accepted control. grading/raster-summary.md.content:
# Independent raster-family adjudication: K27 and X95

Both literal Markdown/JSON reviews match `review-freeze.json`. Assigned source PDFs, briefs, overview renders and the author-a oracle match `input-freeze.json`; source identity also matches each review and frozen oracle. The maintained runtime gate passed before grader PDF opening (Python 3.12.16, pymupdf-lite 2.1, MuPDF 1.28.6; minimum versions only, advisory review still required).

K27 is the frozen clean control. Its actual raster Note 1 reads UTM Zone 11, and both main and locator panels contain their own page-up GRID N arrows. The review makes no discrepancy claim. Its bounded identity, history, adjoining-label, scale, symbol and fill clearances are supported. The different 1:2,000/1:8,000 scales, preliminary Rev 1 history and adjoining NE 14 label were handled in their stated roles.

X95 F01 identifies frozen B-CRS: actual raster Note 1 reads UTM Zone 12 against the brief's Zone 11. F02 identifies frozen B-NORTH: complete source-derived main-panel imagery shows no north graphic or north label, while the separate locator retains its own GRID N arrow. Neither finding relies on native-text absence. No frozen defect was missed; no finding duplicate, unsupported scored assertion, false alarm or bounded false clearance was identified. The unresolved main-orientation restatement earns no detection credit.

Every substantive Markdown assertion is represented in the original JSON, including correction/scope/evidence fields and top-level method records. No Markdown-only finding was added. Kind-preserving normalization accounts for every original claim: K27 has 27 original claims mapped to 50 units; X95 has 30 mapped to 42. Split assertions retain their original parent, kind, qualifications, source identity and evidence; original structured evidence is serialized losslessly as strings for the existing scorer.

Actual whole pages and readable source-derived Notes, titleblock, full main-view and locator/legend crops were inspected. All six raster Notes and both titleblock columns are readable. There is no separate detail, area schedule or total. No material unintended authoring ambiguity or need to revise the frozen oracle was found. Schematic geometry and independent view orientation are explicit; no real-world cadastral adjacency or accepted geometry is inferred.

Saved CLI reports confirm K27's corrected 17 checks (14 PASS / 0 FAIL / 3 REVIEW_REQUIRED) and X95's 13 checks (4 / 0 / 9). K27 retains the initial crop/selection problems and a separate corrected report; comparison of its specifications shows that only ten region selections changed, with expected facts preserved. X95 records inventory serialization, page-size cropping and documentation lookup retries. These technical retries do not alter the frozen completed reports. Raster and graphical CLI limitations remain separate from visual observations.

Saved images, reading records and engine outputs support the reported coverage and results. They cannot independently replay reviewer gaze or authenticate execution chronology. K27's runtime result appears in `tools_used` without a standalone runtime artifact; X95 retains `runtime-security.json`. This is developer/model adjudication of invented drawing QA only. It supports no real-plan accuracy, automatic field discovery, training, current-law, CAD/GIS, survey-control or acceptance claim. The coordinator will run normalization validation and scoring.

Records: `grading/K27/adjudication.json`, `grading/K27/normalized-findings.json`, `grading/X95/adjudication.json`, `grading/X95/normalized-findings.json`. Grader image crops remain in the corresponding grading directories. Original sources, briefs, oracle and literal reviews were not changed.

Overall status: REVIEW_REQUIRED. Regulatory status: NOT_ASSESSED. This bounded drawing review identifies two corrections and does not certify the whole plan or establish regulator acceptance.

Source PDF SHA-256: eaaa7dcea44c50f28dd1531edf8318f5261a2c734f401b42a80a3190b1dd761f. The original PDF was read without modification.

## What was checked

- **M_RUNTIME**: The maintained runtime gate passed before PDF opening, rendering or extraction: MINIMUM_RUNTIME_VERSIONS_ONLY was SATISFIED (Python 3.12.16; pymupdf-lite 2.1; MuPDF 1.28.6). This is not security clearance.

- **M_COVERAGE_1**: PDF page 1 (WEST SEGMENT) was inspected as a whole sheet and in readable titleblock, route and schedule/Notes/footer crops. The complete titleblock and every Notes entry were read top to bottom before selecting QC regions. Border, location strip, route/crossing/match captions, schedule, history/current issue and sheet information were covered; no unread portions remain.

- **M_COVERAGE_2**: PDF page 2 (EAST SEGMENT) was inspected as a whole sheet and in readable titleblock, route and schedule/Notes/footer crops. The complete titleblock and every Notes entry were read top to bottom before selecting QC regions. Border, location strip, route/crossing/match captions, schedule, history/current issue and sheet information were covered; no unread portions remain.

- **M_METHOD**: The finished-plan CLI ran 17 source-bound checks: 13 PASS, 2 FAIL and 2 visual REVIEW_REQUIRED. A technical retry expanded regions to contain overlapping native-font boxes; the first output and retry reason are retained.

- **C01**: Both upper titleblocks identify drawing BT-579-RTF, matching the job brief.

- **C02**: Both upper titleblocks state Rev 1 / 2026-10-30, matching the current issue in the job brief.

- **C03**: The WEST SEGMENT location reads SE 24-064-09 W5M, matching its separate segment location in the job brief.

Use these job facts and all printed sheet information as the review basis. Chainages and scheduled distances are supplied for a schematic route; no surveyed control network, legal boundary reconstruction or current regulatory authority is provided. All names and project information are invented.

- **C25** — The main cabin/access view, wider locator inset, legend, all six Notes, complete two-column titleblock, heading and footer were visually inspected on Sheet 1. No portion of these frames remained unread; no area schedule or numerical total was present to sum. (Sheet 1, whole sheet)

# T67 whole-plan review

Overall status: **REVIEW_REQUIRED**. Regulatory status: **NOT_ASSESSED**.

Two confirmed drawing issues need correction (F01-F02). Source SHA-256: `d740f2556f00aaf7b5dbafe30502dfed9ddfaacf900067e07b8f3ccb256e2ee2`.

## What was checked

The runtime minimum-version check passed before PDF opening. The existing offline CLI then executed five selected drawing checks: two FAIL, one PASS and two REVIEW_REQUIRED. The two unresolved mechanical identity attempts resulted from partially selected native text and were visually checked separately; no rerun changed those results. (M04)

Coverage: The complete single sheet was visually inspected: header and five Drawing Notes, all titleblock cells top to bottom, main diagram and its labels, north arrow, road allowance/access annotations, Detail A, access calculation, historical revision rows and footer. No portions remained unread. (M03)

## What needs attention

- **F01 — Sheet 1, Drawing Notes, entry 3:** Drawing Note 3 cites WI-263 for stockpile operating limits, but the job brief authorizes WI-326 for the current issue. Correct Note 3 to WI-326.
- **F02 — Sheet 1, lower-right Access Length Calculation:** The access total is printed as 211.75 m, but the displayed A 124.50 m and B 86.25 m sum to 210.75 m. The printed total is 1.00 m too high. Correct the total to 210.75 m for the stated parts.

## Bounded checks and observations

- **C01 — Sheet 1, titleblock left, job field:** The visually read titleblock job identifier RWM-26-418 agrees with the job brief.
- **C02 — Sheet 1, titleblock left, drawing field:** The visually read titleblock drawing identifier RM-418-PLA agrees with the job brief.
- **C03 — Sheet 1, titleblock upper-right and lower-right:** Current revision 2 in the titleblock and current revision-record entry agrees with the job brief.
- **C04 — Sheet 1, titleblock upper-right and lower-right:** The current date 2026-10-28 in both current revision entries agrees with the job brief.
- **C05 — Sheet 1, Drawing Notes, entry 1:** Note 1 states SW 14-052-16 W4M, matching the job location.
- **C06 — Sheet 1, Drawing Note 2 and main diagram block labels:** Extraction block Q-2 and stockpile S-1 are separate subjects; the diagram and Note 2 use the identifiers consistently with the brief. Their different identifiers are not a discrepancy.
- **C07 — Sheet 1, main access segment A and lower-right calculation:** The main-diagram segment A label and calculation operand both state 124.50 m.
- **C08 — Sheet 1, main access segment B and lower-right calculation:** The main-diagram segment B label and calculation operand both state 86.25 m.
- **C09 — Sheet 1, titleblock lower-left historical revision record:** WI-281 appears in an explicitly historical revision-1 archive entry dated 2026-09-18; it is not represented as the current operating reference.
- **M01 — Sheet 1, main diagram upper-right and Drawing Note 5:** A visible N-labelled arrow points upward in the main diagram at the upper right; Note 5 describes the bearing reference as illustrative Grid North.
- **M02 — Sheet 1, whole main diagram, Detail A and Drawing Note 4:** No graphical scale bar was found after whole-sheet visual review. Detail A is explicitly schematic with no scale, and Note 4 directs the reader to printed dimensions. No scale requirement or scale defect is asserted for this illustrative exercise.

## What remains unchecked

- **U01:** Survey control acceptance, boundary closure, surveyed area, coordinate alignment and plotted geometry were not verified or reconstructed. The brief and Notes explicitly describe an illustrative diagram without accepted control; no section-quarter fabric or reference-point control network supports those checks.
- **U02:** CAD/GIS geometry, layer mapping and source-to-dataset consistency were not checked because no CAD or GIS artifact was supplied.
- **U03:** Regulatory compliance and current-law applicability were not assessed. The fictional brief supplies no normative requirements or regulator determination, and no external authority was fetched; this review provides no legal, approval or professional acceptance.

## Next steps

Correct Note 3 and the access total as specified in F01 and F02. Any later geometry, CAD/GIS or regulatory assessment needs the separate evidence identified in U01-U03.
